answer: Slow identity creation with a verifiable delay: before an agent can act, it must forge a single-use credential by completing a sequential puzzle that cannot be sped up by running thousands of copies in parallel. Like a willow that bends but cannot be rushed into maturity, each identity takes real wall-clock time to grow, and a sable-marked audit trail records its birth time and first actions. A flood of newborn identities is therefore visible and rate-limited, while established agents continue without friction.
